2026-11-08.title: Hudos Eetho Sunday · Renewal of the Church
readings: My house shall be a house of prayer
Solomon's prayer at the dedication of the Temple
The Lord gathers and renews his people
To the lukewarm Church: I stand at the door and knock
Christ the high priest of the true sanctuary
Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up
2026-11-08.alt: Second Sunday of the liturgical year. (In the lectionary the Book of Revelation is read in the place of the Catholic Epistle.)
2026-11-08.verse: Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.
theo: Last Sunday we celebrated the Church as God's holy dwelling. Today, Hudos Eetho, we celebrate her renewal. The two belong together. The Church is holy because Christ sanctifies her, yet she is made of sinners and is always in need of purification. The Second Vatican Council says it plainly: the Church, “holding sinners in her bosom, is at the same time holy and always in need of being purified” (Lumen Gentium 8).

The readings show both the danger and the remedy. At the foot of Sinai the people make a golden calf, worshipping a god they can control. Solomon, dedicating the Temple, admits that “heaven and the highest heaven cannot contain you, much less this house that I have built” (1 Kings 8:27). God's house can never be our possession. The risen Christ says to the Church of Laodicea: “Because you are lukewarm… I am about to spit you out of my mouth” (Revelation 3:16). The danger of a Church is not only sin but comfort.

Jesus enters the Temple with a whip of cords and drives out the traders. His anger is not against worship but against worship turned into business. Then he points to himself: “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.” He was speaking of the temple of his body. The true renewal of the Church is always a return to Christ, crucified and risen, whose blood, says Hebrews, purifies “our conscience from dead works to worship the living God” (Hebrews 9:14).

Renewal does not come from outside the Church but from her own sources: the Word, the Mysteries, prayer and repentance. That is why the Lord, after rebuking Laodicea, says: “Listen! I am standing at the door, knocking; if you hear my voice and open the door, I will come in to you and eat with you.”
conn: The golden calf and the Lamb.
Israel melted gold to make a god they could see. In Christ, God gives himself visibly, not as gold but as the Lamb whose blood cleanses (Hebrews 9:12).
“A house of prayer for all peoples.”
Jesus quotes Isaiah 56:7 and Jeremiah 7:11. The traders filled the Court of the Gentiles, the one place where the nations could pray.
John 2:21 is fulfilled at the Resurrection; the Church, his Body, becomes the temple where God is worshipped “in spirit and truth” (John 4:23).
Isaiah 55:1 invites the thirsty to buy “without money”; the free gift of grace flows from the side of Christ, the new Temple (Ezekiel 47:1; John 19:34).
altar: “I will come in to you and eat with you” (Revelation 3:20). At every Holy Qurbono the Lord who cleansed the Temple enters his Church and shares his table with us. Renewal begins at the altar, in a worthy and fervent communion, and spreads from there into the parish.
outline: Ask: if Jesus walked into our parish today, what would he praise, and what would he overturn?
Point 1 · Holy, yet always being purified
Lumen Gentium 8: the Church is holy and always in need of renewal. This is honesty, not shame.
Point 2 · The two dangers: idols and lukewarmness
The golden calf: a God we control. Laodicea: a Church that is comfortable. Name today's forms of both.
Point 3 · Renewal is a return to Christ
“Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.” Renewal comes from the risen Lord, through the Word, the Mysteries and repentance.
The Lord standing at the door and knocking: he wants to come in and eat with us.
“Lord, renew your Church, and begin with me.”
live: Name one thing that takes God's place in your life, and set a limit to it this week.
Make a good Confession this month, and prepare well for Holy Qurbono next Sunday.
Arrive early for Qurbono and keep silence in church as a sign of reverence.
fathers: Commenting on John 2, he says the temple Jesus will raise is his body, and that the whole Church, as the body of Christ, will be raised and built as a living temple (Commentary on John 10).
He warns that the Lord enters each soul as he entered the Temple, and asks whether we have made it a house of prayer or a market (Homilies on John 23).
magis: The Church, embracing sinners in her bosom, is at the same time holy and always in need of purification, and follows constantly the path of penance and renewal.
Christ summons the Church to continual reformation, of which she always has need, insofar as she is a human institution.
All members of the Church, including her ministers, must acknowledge that they are sinners; the Church therefore gathers sinners and is called to holiness.
saints: Consult the 2026–27 lectionary for the commemorations of this week. In the 2025–26 lectionary, St Theodore was remembered on this Sunday.
2026-11-08.prayer: Lord Jesus, you cleansed the Temple and raised up the temple of your body. Purify your Church, free us from idols and lukewarmness, and come in to eat with us at your holy table. Amen.

quick: The Church is holy and always in need of renewal.
Two dangers: idols we control and comfortable lukewarmness.
Renewal is always a return to the crucified and risen Christ.
2026-11-08.action: Name one idol in your life and set a limit to it this week.
2026-11-08.question: What would Jesus overturn in my life if he walked in today?
2026-11-08.special: Hudos Eetho Sunday: the renewal (dedication) of the Church; the second Sunday of the Syro-Malankara liturgical year.
illus: An old church in a Kerala town is repainted and repaired every few decades; the building stays the same but is renewed. Every Christian generation must renew the Church in the same way: not by changing the faith, but by returning to its source.

family.explain: Jesus is like a friend standing at our door and knocking. If we open, he comes in and eats with us. We open the door by praying and by coming to Holy Qurbono.
family.intention: We pray that our Church may be renewed and that lukewarm hearts may become fervent.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we open the door to Jesus this week?”

catechism: Renewal and the holiness of the Church.
kidsaint: She saw how many people were thirsty for love and opened her door to them. She often said Jesus' words on the cross: “I thirst.” Lesson: open your door to Jesus and to people who need you.
term: Syriac for “the renewal” or dedication of the Church. The second Sunday of the year, following Qudos Eetho. Together they open the year with the mystery of the Church.
termMore: Why is the Book of Revelation read here?
In the Syro-Malankara lectionary, readings from Revelation can take the place of the Catholic Epistle. The letters to the seven Churches are a fitting word for the renewal of the Church.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, last Sunday we celebrated the Church as God's holy house. Today, Hudos Eetho, we celebrate the renewal of the Church. Both are true at once: the Church is holy because Christ makes her holy, and she is always in need of renewal because she is made of us, sinners.

Our readings show two dangers. At Sinai the people made a golden calf, a god they could see and control. And the risen Lord says to the Church of Laodicea: “Because you are lukewarm, I will spit you out of my mouth.” The danger of the Church is not only sin, but comfort.

Then Jesus enters the Temple and overturns the tables of the traders. He was not against worship; he was against worship turned into business. And he said: “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.” He was speaking of his body. Every true renewal of the Church is a return to Christ, crucified and risen.

So where does renewal begin? Not with someone else. With me. With a good Confession, with silence and reverence in church, with a heart that opens when the Lord knocks. “If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in and eat with him.” In a few moments he will do exactly that at this altar. Amen.
kids: Children, what happens if nobody cleans the house for a long time? Dust everywhere! Jesus once went into the Temple and cleaned it, because people had made it a market.
Our hearts are God's house too. We clean them by saying sorry to Jesus and by praying. Jesus says: “I am standing at your door, knocking.” Shall we open the door to him? Let's say: “Come in, Jesus!”

intro: Theme: “Renew the house of God, beginning with yourself.”

Last Sunday we celebrated the Church as God's holy dwelling. Today, Hudos Eetho, the Church asks to be renewed. Jesus enters the Temple, drives out the traders and speaks of a new temple, his own body. Renewal is not a new building or a new programme; it is a return to God.

sub: Jesus makes a whip and overturns the tables: he will not allow God's house to become a market.
At Sinai the people exchanged the living God for a golden calf; idols always creep into the house of God.
Our idols today: money, status, rivalry and noise in God's house, and the busy “trade” in our own hearts.
q: And they said, “These are your gods, O Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt!”
He told those who were selling the doves, “Take these things out of here! Stop making my Father's house a marketplace!”
points.apply: Name one idol that crowds God out of your heart, and remove it this week.

sub: Solomon knew that no building could contain God.
Jesus says: “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up”: he speaks of his body.
Through his body, crucified and risen, we meet God; in Baptism we become members of that body, the Church.
q: But will God indeed dwell on the earth? Even heaven and the highest heaven cannot contain you, much less this house that I have built!
Jesus answered them, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.” … But he was speaking of the temple of his body.
points.apply: Before Holy Qurbono, remember: you are entering the body of Christ, and you will receive him into your own.

sub: Moses interceded and God relented; there is always a way back.
Isaiah invites: “Seek the LORD while he may be found.”
The risen Christ knocks at the door of a lukewarm Church; renewal is opening the door to him.
q: Seek the LORD while he may be found, call upon him while he is near; let the wicked forsake their way, and the unrighteous their thoughts; let them return to the LORD, that he may have mercy on them.
Listen! I am standing at the door, knocking; if you hear my voice and open the door, I will come in to you and eat with you, and you with me.
points.apply: Make a good confession before the Annunciation season advances.

concl: The Church is renewed when each of us is renewed. Jesus still cleanses the temple, not with a whip of cords now, but with his word and his sacraments.
Let us open the door to him, cast out our idols, and become again a house of prayer for all peoples.
2026-11-08.resolve: Spend ten minutes in silence in church this week, asking: “Lord, what must you cleanse in me?”
